chapter: Trumpet technique: breath, lip and effects
title: Odd lip positions: Petit, Pop Celestin and Young Kid Punch
summary: Punch demonstrates how Buddy Petit, Celestin and Young Kid Punch placed the horn on the lip.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Oh, oh, oh. What are some of the other different ways that guys had of lipping their horns?

Well, Buddy Petit lived way on the side here. On his right side? Right side, yeah. Right side. Right there. Just like that. That's where he played. And if anybody noticed Pop Silistan, he put this part in front, but the bottom part around here. That's what he used to play like. Like that.
Yeah. He'd twist his mouth all around.
Put the mouthpiece on the front and down here on the bottom.
He'd twist his mouth all around.

And we had a fellow here, called himself Young Kid Punch. He fell dead there at Ramport and Tulane Avenue. Going somewhere to play. I was out the lake. And he played like this. Let me see how he played. With his horn pointing up. Oh, just up there. Just a little bit of this.
Turn around to the side a little bit. Now that's about a thirty degree angle up, huh? Mm-hmm. Maybe forty-five, something like that. You never did know his real name like this, yeah?
